Head of Compliance – help us build a bank Europe can trust

We are looking for a Head of Compliance who sees regulation as part of how a bank is built, and part of its culture.

As a senior professional you are to become our Head of Compliance and Data Protection Responsible. Someone who knows the craft inside out, and would - if faced with a choice - choose to shape a smarter, leaner and specific compliance function over a more broad based big-bank machine.

As part of our second line of defence, you lead the Compliance function with overall responsibility for identifying, assessing, monitoring, advising on and reporting on compliance and data risks.

This is a rare opportunity to shape the governance and compliance culture of a fast-growing bank at an early stage. You work closely with Executive Management and the Board of Directors, and your judgement directly influences how we grow across Denmark, and the rest of the EU. If you pair deep regulatory expertise with integrity and a commercial mindset, this is a place where you can make a real difference.

What you will be doing

Compliance framework & monitoring

• You run and ensure timely development of our effective compliance framework (incl. Compliance AI) based on the bank’s business model and risk appetite, including the annual compliance risk assessment, the multi-year compliance review plan and the Compliance Procedure.

• You review and monitor the effectiveness of the bank’s methods and procedures across all areas relevant to financial regulation – including financial crime prevention (AML/CTF, sanctions, fraud, ABC), credit, DORA, GDPR, solvency and capital (CRR/CRD), PSD2/PSD3 and MiCA.

• You report regularly to Executive Management and the Board of Directors, and escalate significant findings, warnings or concerns when compliance risks or incidents arise.

Regulation & business development

• You monitor new and updated regulation, assess its impact on the bank and advise on implementation together with Legal.

• You take part in our business development process: reviewing new products, assessing new outsourcing and overseeing product governance.

• You take part in meetings with the Danish FSA and other supervisory authorities, and follow up on any remediation.

Data protection

• You take on the role as kompasbank’s Data Protection Responsible: the contact point for data protection authorities and data subjects, handling breach reporting and access requests, and advising on data processing agreements, transfer impact assessments and DPIAs.

Governance & culture

• You own our whistleblower scheme and case handling.

• You advise on the Remuneration Policy and supporting Executive Management on investor relations and equity and debt financing.

• You build a strong risk and compliance culture through training and awareness, and making sure the Compliance function has the resources it needs.

• Working closely with Risk Management to coordinate second-line reviews and risk assessments.

What we expect from you

• Legal background: A law degree (cand.jur., cand.merc.jur. or equivalent) and 10+ years of experience in financial services, with solid experience from a bank, a law firm, a fintech or a supervisory authority.

• Compliance expertise: Proven experience leading or holding a senior role in a compliance function in a regulated financial institution.

• Regulatory knowledge: Strong analytical capability within Danish and EU financial regulation, procedures and products; knowledge of the Danish Financial Business Act and Executive Order on Management and Control of Banks, etc., AML/CTF, DORA and MiCA is a strong plus.

• Data protection: Knowledge of GDPR and data protection practice in a regulated environment; experience from a data protection role is a strong plus.

• Collaboration and communication: You build strong relationships across the bank and explain complex regulation clearly to colleagues, management and regulators.

As Head of Compliance is a key function, the position is subject to a fit & proper assessment by kompasbank and the Danish FSA. You must therefore be able to document sufficient knowledge, experience and a good reputation, and have no criminal record or ongoing insolvency proceedings that could affect your suitability.

What we offer

• A key leadership role with real influence and a direct line to Executive Management and the Board.

• A high-energy, collaborative work culture built on trust, humor, ambition, and innovation.

• Competitive salary, attractive pension scheme, six weeks of paid holiday, and comprehensive health insurance.

• 60+ skilled, ambitious, and friendly colleagues.

• A modern office in beautiful green surroundings in Vedbæk, north of Copenhagen.

• Ongoing learning and development opportunities.

About kompasbank

Europe runs on small and medium-sized businesses. SMEs make up 99% of all EU companies, employ around 100 million people and generate more than half of Europe’s GDP. Yet they are the part of the economy that the financial system serves worst: too complex for automated retail credit, too small to be worth a traditional corporate bank’s attention. The Draghi report on European competitiveness was blunt. Europe is falling behind the US and China in growth, productivity and technology, and fragmented, slow-moving capital is a central reason why. Europe will not become relevant again through a handful of champions alone. It needs thousands of ambitious mid-sized companies that can get financing, move money domestically and internationally, and scale across borders as easily as their American competitors. That is where kompasbank stands. Built on a full EU banking licence, we bank European SMEs properly, with serious service, data excellence and the regulatory rigour that lets us say yes where others say no.

We’re a cloud-native neobank with no legacy systems and no silos. Since opening our doors in August 2021, we’ve grown fast, expanding across Denmark, Germany and Spain, with a growth rate of more than 1,150% and top rankings on the Sifted lists – and we were named Best Bank for SMEs – Denmark 2024 by FDI Insider.

Job Description

At Netcompany, we are looking for both newly graduated candidates with a relevant master’s degree – or equivalent experience – who want to work as IT Consultants at the intersection of technology, business, and people. Do you want to help develop some of Denmark’s most complex and business-critical IT solutions, where software development, project management, and close client collaboration are central parts of everyday work?

Responsibilities and technologies

As an IT Consultant, you help translate client needs into the right technical solution. We choose the technologies that best fit each project and client. As a result, you should enjoy working across a variety of technologies and domains, while continuously expanding your knowledge and expertise.

A large part of our projects is based on web technologies such as Angular or React, and Java or C# on either a Java or .NET platform. In addition, we work with a wide range of standard platforms including Microsoft, Salesforce, IBM, Oracle, Adobe, Snowflake, Guidewire, and others.

As an IT Consultant, you contribute to all parts of system development with a focus on technical tasks. Your responsibilities will vary from project to project and evolve over time, but your responsibilites will typically include:

• Setting up and developing frameworks and integrations.

• Implementing features in user interfaces.

• Configuring and developing extensions for standard platforms.

• Automating business processes, for example through batch jobs.

• Developing tools and scripts for migrating large volumes of data.

You will join a team with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and areas of expertise. What we all have in common is a technical mindset and shared ambition to build the best possible IT solutions together.

Our projects include some of Denmark’s most innovative and mission-critical IT initiatives across the public and private sectors, meaning you will help shape and improve everyday life for a large part of society.

About you

We expect you to hold a masters's degree in engineering, computer science, software, IT, or a similar field. To succeed in this role, you:

• Are a recent graduate or have a couple of years of experience – most importantly, you are passionate about taking your IT career to the next level.

• Possess strong technical skills in object-oriented programming.

• Have a solid understanding of software development and motivated to further develop your skills.

• Think analytically, show initiative, and work in a structured way.

• Full professional proficiency in Swedish and English (written and spoken) is a must. As you will be working closely with Danish clients and colleagues, you should be able to communicate and collaborate effectively in a Danish work environment.

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

This is a unique opportunity to join a newly established AI function and shape how AI becomes part of the way we work. As the first person in this role, you will help build the foundation for future growth while working closely with the Central AI team and stakeholders across the business.

We are looking for someone who combines strong business understanding with the ability to drive change and inspire others. You are comfortable working across functions, navigating ambiguity, and helping colleagues understand how AI can support their goals.

You bring a practical and collaborative approach, and you enjoy turning new technologies into meaningful business outcomes.

Would you like to turn structure, analysis and practical coordination into more effective crisis readiness? Join TDC NET and help maintain and develop the framework, tools and training that support our Crisis Management Team.

TDC NET owns and operates digital infrastructure that is critical to Denmark. Our Crisis Management framework helps the organisation respond when serious events require fast coordination, clear decisions and reliable communication. You will join the Business Continuity and Crisis Management area and work closely with experienced colleagues and stakeholders across the organisation.

About the job

We are looking for a motivated and structured student assistant who wants to learn how crisis readiness is built in practice. You will support both the day-to-day maintenance of our Crisis Management framework and the continued development of the Crisis Management Team. The role combines practical coordination, document and data management, analysis, communication and continuous improvement work.

You will receive clear priorities and guidance, but you will also be trusted to be responsible for defined tasks and follow them through. Your work will contribute directly to making plans easier to use, training more effective, and improvement actions more visible.

Purpose of the role

Your purpose is to help keep our crisis-management setup current, organised and ready for use. You will support documents, exercises, readiness activities, reporting and follow-up, while learning how operational resilience and executive crisis management work in a large infrastructure company.

Key responsibilities

• Maintain and improve crisis plans, appendices, role descriptions, quick guides, checklists and templates.

• Coordinate practical preparation for workshops, activation drills and crisis exercises, including invitations, rooms, Teams setup, materials and participant data.

• Collect and structure data from training, activations and exercises, and prepare clear overviews and PowerPoint material.

• Maintain action and improvement trackers, follow up with owners and prepare concise status updates.

• Support stronger decision logging, situation reporting, briefing flows and role-ready crisis-room materials.

• Carry out desk research on crisis management, operational resilience, emerging risks and best practice.

• Help explore, test and responsibly apply AI to improve crisis preparedness, response, recovery, decision and action logging, situation reporting and post-incident learning.

What you will work on from the start

Recent exercises have identified practical opportunities to make activation faster, clarify interfaces, improve decision and situation reporting. We also want to explore how responsible use of AI can improve crisis preparedness, response, recovery, reporting and continuous learning. You will help turn these lessons into updated tools, training material, trackers and follow-up activities. You will support the work, while decisions and formal ownership remain with the relevant specialists and leaders.

Your first months

During your first months, you will learn the Crisis Management framework, key roles, exercise cycle and improvement backlog. With support from the team, you will gradually take ownership of recurring practical tasks, selected improvement actions and clearly defined deliverables. You will be expected to keep overviews current, flag issues early, and ask for guidance when decisions or sensitive information are involved.

The role is designed to combine learning with real responsibility. You will work close to both operational specialists and senior stakeholders, but you will not make crisis decisions or replace specialist role holders. Your contribution is to make the process, tools, information and follow-up more reliable and easier to use.

“You will not just help maintain documents. You will help us turn lessons from exercises into practical improvements that enhance how the organisation prepares, coordinates and responds to a crisis.”

- Noah Fröhlich, Head of Business Continuity, TDC NET

About you

We imagine that you:

• Are enrolled in a relevant higher-education programme, for example emergency and risk management, security, political science, business, engineering, communication, law or a similar field.

• Work in a structured way, pay attention to detail and reliably finish what you start.

• Can turn complex information into clear notes, simple overviews and well-structured slides.

• Are curious, proactive and comfortable asking questions when something is unclear.

• Are skilled using Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel and Word, or motivated to become so quickly.

• Have AI fluency, practical experience with AI tools or a genuine interest in learning how AI can be used responsibly in crisis management.

• Communicate fluently in English, both in writing and verbally.

• Can handle sensitive information responsibly and exercise sound judgement.

• Are able to obtain and maintain the security clearance required for the position. Employment will be conditional on successful security approval.

• Can work approximately 15–20 hours per week, with flexibility around exam periods.

Previous experience with crisis management is not required. We value your structure, judgement, curiosity and willingness to learn.

What you will gain

• Practical experience with crisis management, business continuity and operational resilience in critical infrastructure.

• Insight into how executive teams prepare for and manage serious incidents.

• Experience planning exercises, analysing results and converting lessons into practical improvements.

• Enhanced capabilities in structured problem solving, project coordination, data analysis and executive communication.

• Close collaboration with experienced colleagues across technology, security, operations, communications, legal and senior management.

• The opportunity to take real responsibility for defined deliverables and see the impact of your work.

As a Solution Engineer – Privileged Access Management (PAM) & Identity Infrastructure at TDC NET, you will play a key role in designing, implementing, and operating enterprise Identity and Privileged Access Management solutions. You will be responsible for securing privileged access across infrastructure, applications, cloud platforms, and operational technology while ensuring seamless integration with Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, PKI, and modern automation practices.

About the job

Working closely with Infrastructure, Security, Platform Engineering, and Application teams, you will help automate identity services, improve security controls, and improve operational efficiency through Infrastructure-as-Code and modern engineering practices.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Design, implement, configure, and maintain enterprise PAM solutions.

• Integrate servers, applications, databases, network devices, and cloud platforms into the PAM ecosystem.

• Manage and support Microsoft Active Directory, Entra ID , LDAP, MFA and related identity services.

• Support and maintain Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), including certificate lifecycle management and secure authentication mechanisms.

• Automate PAM and identity-related processes using Infrastructure-as-Code and scripting.

• Monitor platform performance, troubleshoot complex technical issues, and continuously improve platform stability and security.

• Identify security risks and implement mitigation strategies aligned with enterprise security standards.

• Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing across engineering teams.

"We are building more than an IAM platform. We are building a modern identity engineering capability. If you enjoy solving complex security challenges, driving automation, and making a real impact, you'll fit right in with our team."

– Abhishek Kumar, Senior Manager – Identity & Access Management, TDC NET

About you

You are passionate about Identity & Access Management, infrastructure security, and automation. You enjoy solving complex technical challenges and continuously improving enterprise security platforms through modern engineering practices.

You thrive in collaborative environments where Security, Infrastructure, Cloud, and DevOps come together to build secure and scalable identity services.

Required Qualifications

• 4+ years of experience working with Identity & Access Management (IAM), Privileged Access Management (PAM), or Security Infrastructure.

SmallClaims – turning unpaid invoices into won court cases Every year, European businesses write off billions in valid, winnable claims. Oktogrid

Oktogrid™ is helping electricity providers bring the grid online for higher reliability and a safer energy transition. The future will be electric, Oktogrid™ is giving the insights needed to keep the power flowing. We are a dedicated team working with industry heavyweights in optimising the usage of the electrical grid and making sure that the electrification of our society remains sustainable.

The Mission

Phanofi is a DTU spin-out building the next generation of optical communication infrastructure. We design integrated photonic interconnect chips that reduce power consumption and increase data throughput for AI datacenters, quantum computing, and space applications.

Getting photonic integrated circuits (PICs) out of the lab and into packaged, manufacturable modules is one of the hardest problems in our field, and often the one that decides whether a promising chip becomes a product. As a diverse team of 16, we are at an inflection point, growing our engineering capability to take our photonic interconnect technology from prototype toward scalable, production-ready products.

As Senior Photonics Packaging Engineer, you own that transition. You will work in tight collaboration with our electronic, R&D and photonic engineers and our CTO, with real influence over technical direction as we scale.

Key Responsibilities

You own the packaging of our PICs end to end: turning a functional die into a robust, manufacturable module. In practice that spans the optical interface (fiber attach, alignment and bonding), the electrical interface (from DC and control lines through to high-speed RF interconnect), and the substrate or interposer that ties them together, glass, silicon, ceramic or organic. Few people have worked on all of these in equal depth, and we don't expect you to have. We do expect you to understand how a choice in one area constrains the others, and to be able to reason through the trade-offs with us.

Alongside the builds, you'll advance our packaging methods from bench-level assembly toward repeatable, pilot-production-ready processes, characterise what you build yourself and use the results to debug and refine, and bring packaging constraints upstream into design reviews so that packageability and yield are designed in rather than fixed later. You'll also help establish engineering and characterisation processes that suit a small, fast-moving team today and still hold up as we grow.

What We Are Looking For

• 
Experience: 5+ years in photonics engineering with deep, hands-on expertise in advanced PIC packaging. Demonstrated ownership of at least one packaging technology from lab prototype toward pilot production is highly preferred.

• 
Technical Background: A strong engineering or scientific background in photonics, integrated optics or a related field, with genuine hands-on advanced PIC packaging experience. You should have a working understanding of the breadth of modern packaging, optical coupling and attach, high-speed RF and DC electrical interfaces, and interposer and substrate technologies, even where your own depth sits in one or two of them. Working knowledge of optical characterisation methods and instrumentation, and comfort interpreting the data yourself, is essential.

• 
Education: A master's or Ph.D. in Photonics, Optical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field.

• 
Nice to have: Photonic design or modelling experience, comfort running simulations to inform packaging trade-offs, reliability qualification experience, or experience working with external foundry, substrate or assembly partners.

• 
Collaboration & Communication: You are a clear communicator who can engage both engineering peers and leadership on technical trade-offs. You are comfortable operating with autonomy and thrive in a small, collaborative, fast-paced deep-tech environment.

The Perks

We care about your long-term growth and well-being. We offer performance-based stock options, healthcare insurance, professional development support, and a positive culture with free snacks. jobs.description:
We are looking for one or two highly motivated research assistants for 4-month period to investigate how a long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) variant of ASCC3 regulates transcriptional recovery following DNA damage, in the Svejstrup lab, DNRF Center of Excellence, Center for Gene Expression (CGEN), Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM), Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. Staring date: January 1, 2027

  Previous work from the Svejstrup group identified two gene products of ASCC3 implicated in this response: a protein, encoded by the long mRNA transcript, that suppresses transcription during the late stages of the UV-induced global shutdown; and a short mRNA transcript that acts as a regulatory lncRNA, suppressing the ASCC3 protein's function and enabling transcriptional recovery.

  The project will be focused on understanding how the ASCC3 lncRNA regulates RNAPII-mediated transcription and its recovery after DNA damage, using CRISPR/Cas9 technologies to generate and manipulate ASCC3 transcript variants, combined with state-of-the-art transcription profiling approaches such as TTchem-seq and RNA-seq.

  Information on the Department can be found at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/ 

   

  Our Center and Research
 CGEN is an interdisciplinary research center consisting of 6 research groups located in modern laboratories in the Mærsk Tower at the Panum Institute. Our mission is to use a cutting-edge ensemble of genetic, cell biological, biochemical, organismal, and modern ‘omic’-approaches to achieve a comprehensive understanding of the process of gene expression.

  CGEN performs ground-breaking research in a collaborative and ambitious environment, where young researchers are offered the best conditions to engage in bold and imaginative research. CGEN is also a center of learning, where PhDs and postdocs receive comprehensive insights in the cellular processes underlying gene expression, as well as a clear view of their medical importance and potential for a future research carreer.

jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), invites applications for a fully funded 3-year PhD-position from 1 May 2027 or after agreement.  
 
 The position and the project
 The successful candidate will work on the project Treatments for Complex PTSD (RECONNECT-trial), a randomized controlled trial conducted in the Mental Health Services. The project has a strong focus on patient involvement and investigating mechanisms of change within the three intervention arms (Prolonged Exposure, Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing and Enhanced Emotional and Interpersonal Skills Training). The project is conducted in collaboration between researchers in psychology and psychiatry.
 
 Duties and responsibilities
 The PhD student will be central in the research project, being involved in and responsible for large parts of the data collection. Most importantly, the PhD-student will be responsible for conceptualizing and conducting a subset of studies. As such, data management and data analyses, as well as manuscript preparation and communication of research results to the scientific community as well as to relevant stakeholders will be central.

  The PhD-student will be responsible for the assessment of the participants with the International Trauma Interview in Danish, overseeing recruitment progress, and conducting quantitative and qualitative research based on survey and interview data. Experience with quantitative and qualitative data analysis is a must. The candidate must have strong clinical skills and preferably with trauma populations. The candidate must be able to work independently under supervision. Collaborative skills and team spirit are in high regard. For the right candidate, there will be ample possibilities to influence the project and develop new project ideas within the project frame.

 The PhD-student will be part of a research group at the Department of Psychology conducting psychological and psychiatric research on psychotherapy and trauma.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral researcher in environmental microbial ecology
jobs.description:
The Department of Biology, Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a two-year, fixed-term postdoctoral position in environmental microbial ecology, starting 1 February, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is part of a project funded by the Villum Foundation's Villum Experiment programme.

The project
Electrically conductive iron minerals are widespread in anoxic aquatic sediments, yet we know little about the microorganisms that live on them. The project aims to characterize the phylogenetic identity and ecophysiology of microorganisms associated with these minerals. We hypothesize that, by facilitating extracellular electron transfer, the minerals provide a distinct niche that selectively enriches electroactive microorganisms relative to the surrounding sediment.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two–year position from 1 February, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 
This is a fixed-term position to end on 31 January, 2029.

Job description
You will identify, visualize and characterize bacterial and archaeal cells associated with iron minerals by combining fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and correlative imaging, DNA- and/or RNA-based omics, and stable isotope incubation experiments. You will have considerable freedom to shape the methodological approach and to develop your own ideas within the project framework. Project collaborators in Germany will contribute chemical characterization of the minerals, giving you the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary team. Participation in supervision of BSc., MSc. and PhD students and possibly some classroom teaching is also expected.

Your profile
You hold a PhD in biology, earth and environmental science, biotechnology or a related field (or expect to complete it before the start date), and you have a research background in microbiology or microbial ecology.

Essentials:

• Experience with advanced microscopy and/or molecular microbial ecology methods.
• Interest in microbial physiology and electromicrobiology.
• A systematic approach to method development and testing.
• A publication record in international peer-reviewed journals, relative to your career stage.
• Very good written and oral communication skills in English.
Desirable:

• Experience with FISH, correlative microscopy, stable isotope probing, or omics data analysis.
• Experience working with sediment or other environmental samples.
• Experience with microbial physiology and/or electromicrobiology.
• If you are excited about the project but your experience does not match every point, we still encourage you to apply.
At the Department of Biology, we value a collegial and inclusive working environment and place strong emphasis on good relationships among colleagues and students. We welcome colleagues who bring an open, constructive and collaborative approach.

Who we are
The Department of Biology (Aarhus University) provides a framework for research and teaching in all major biological subdisciplines. The department currently encompasses approximately 200 academic and technical staff and 45 PhD students while 400 students follow the BSc and MSc programs offered by the department. The Section for Microbiology (https://bio.au.dk/en/about-biology/sections/microbiology) employs 12 associate and full professors and offers a vibrant, international research environment for studying microbial physiology, evolution, ecology, and biogeochemistry. The section integrates basic and applied research, addressing the functions, eco-physiology, and evolution of microorganisms in natural and biotechnological systems. The section has well-equipped laboratories, a permanent support staff of highly skilled laboratory technicians, and access to advanced imaging facilities on the AU campus.

What we offer
• A two-year position in a stimulating, international research environment
• Access to state-of-the-art laboratories and imaging facilities.
• A work environment encouraging lively, open and critical discussion.
• A work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities.
• A workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Aarhus University, and the place of employment is Section for Microbiology within the Department of Biology (https://bio.au.dk/en/), Aarhus University, Ny Munkegade 114, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contact information
Applicants seeking further information are invited to contact Assoc. Prof. Kasper Urup Kjeldsen at AU (kasperuk@bio.au.dk).

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 29 November, 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.
